title: Conventional birth date; birthplace disputed
description: Later scholarship conventionally dates Bulleh Shah's birth to about 1680, but traditions disagree between Uch Gillanian/the Bahawalpur region and Pandoke or the Qasur region.

title: Family associated with Pandoke
description: Traditional accounts say the family settled in Pandoke, where Bulleh Shah's father served the mosque and taught village children. Exact dates and the sequence of moves are not securely documented.

date_label: Youth or early adulthood; exact date unknown
title: Higher education traditionally placed in Kasur
description: Later sources place Bulleh Shah's higher education in Kasur and associate it with Arabic, Persian, Quranic, legal, and Sufi literary learning. Teacher and curriculum details need verification.

title: Discipleship under Shah Inayat Qadiri
description: Multiple sources and poetic references associate Bulleh Shah with the Lahore-based Shah Inayat Qadiri as murshid. Stories of their first meeting vary and should be treated as hagiographic traditions.

title: Post-Aurangzeb instability in Punjab
description: Bulleh Shah's adult life is situated by modern scholarship amid short Mughal reigns, political fragmentation, and repeated invasions affecting Punjab. This is historical context, not proof that a particular poem directly refers to a specific event.

title: Death and burial tradition at Kasur
description: The conventional death date is 1757, with 1758 also appearing in catalog records. His shrine and continuing public commemoration are located in Kasur.
